name: Icon
description: Box props on an icon somebody else drew — lucide, Tabler, react-icons, an Iconify set, a raw `<svg>`. It clones the one element it is given and puts the engine's class on it, so it knows no icon set's API and the class beats the `width`/`height` the set writes for itself.

props.name: children
props.description: The icon: exactly one element, whose `<svg>` these props are styling.

props.name: size
props.description: Width and height at once, on the ÷4 scale: `size={6}` is the 24px an icon set defaults to, and is the default here too. It wins over `width`/`height`. Careful when porting — a set's own `size` is in pixels.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the icon — `role="img"` and this text. Without one the icon is `aria-hidden`.

props.name: props
props.description: Attributes forwarded to the icon's element, over anything the icon writes for itself.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles forwarded to the icon's element. Box props are the way to style it; this is for a value that has to be computed per render, which no class can hold.

a11y: An icon with no `label` is `aria-hidden`, which is right for the common case: the icon repeats a label that is already there, and reading it twice is noise.
A `label` makes it `role="img"` with that text as its name — for an icon that is the only thing saying what a control does.
